summary: Feed s064_single to IDS is degraded: 21.8% of TCP sessions (41/188) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional traffic for reassembly. All other visibility checks (drops, overload, truncation, duplicates, tunnels, VLAN, encryption, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction for ~22% of flows. Most likely cause is incomplete aggregation - TAP/SPAN source covers only one side of asymmetrically routed path, or broker policy/filter is forwarding only client-to-server (or server-to-client) to this IDS port so return traffic never arrives. Not caused by drops or overload (both healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true and needs_full_payload=true for TCP stream reassembly, state tracking and signature matching. With one-way sessions the IDS cannot reconstruct flows, misses exploits, C2 and lateral movement, and produces incomplete session logs leading to false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both forward and reverse directions from all relevant TAP/SPAN sources and forward with 5-tuple flow affinity to this IDS port. This restores bidirectional session visibility required for IDS detection without creating duplicates or overload.
